Hi Melanie — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a compact worked example and the key commercial terms. See attached appendix + token matrix for full line items.

Summary (high level)
- Provisioned burst pool: sold as "burst credits" (token-equivalent credits) that are prepaid monthly. They act as a top-up to the commit and are consumed before overage pricing is applied. The pool is priced as a mixed product: a small monthly reservation fee (capacity credit) + per-token draw cost only when used.
- Variable anchoring (overage rate): overage per-token price is anchored to the committed effective per-token rate (commit spend / committed tokens). Anchor acts as a floor; overage uses a tiered uplift depending on how far above commit you go. We provide deterministic multipliers and a smoothing true-up.

Key commercial terms (proposed)
- Baseline commit: 25M tokens / month at an effective blended rate of $0.0009/token (monthly commit invoice = $22,500).
- Provisioned burst pool: Option A — 5M prepaid burst credits/month. Fee structure: $3,000/month reservation + $0.0006 per burst-token consumed. Unused burst credits expire at month-end (or can be rolled into a one-month buffer with a 25% retention fee).
- Overage pricing (post-burst): tiered multipliers applied to baseline effective rate:
  - 0–20% above commit: 1.15x baseline ($0.001035/token)
  - 20–50% above commit: 1.35x baseline ($0.001215/token)
  - >50% above commit: 1.75x baseline ($0.001575/token)
- Invoice smoothing / true-up: monthly billing uses provisional per-token calculations. A quarterly true-up reconciles provisional burst reservation credits and actual consumption; surplus is credited or shortfall invoiced.

Worked example (June)
- Baseline commit: 25,000,000 tokens
- Provisioned burst prepaid: 5,000,000 burst credits (reservation fee $3,000)
- Actual consumption: 31,250,000 tokens
  - Step 1: Commit covers first 25,000,000 tokens at $0.0009 -> $22,500
  - Step 2: Use prepaid burst credits for next 5,000,000 tokens at $0.0006 -> $3,000 (note reservation fee already paid)
  - Step 3: Remaining overage: 1,250,000 tokens above commit+burst -> compute uplift segment: this is 5% above commit+burst (1,250,000 / 25,000,000 = 5%) so falls in 0–20% band -> 1.15x baseline = $0.001035 -> overage charge = $1,293.75
  - June invoice (tokens only): $22,500 + $3,000 + $1,293.75 = $26,793.75

Notes on roll-forward and notice windows
- Default: prepaid burst credits expire month-end.
- Optional: for enterprise customers with annual commit, we can enable a 1-month roll buffer (up to 25% of monthly burst) for a 25% retention fee to preserve unused burst credits for the following month.
- Burst capacity increase lead time: typical immediate (API-driven) for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private, we require 72 hours for capacity spin-up and a 14-day notice for guaranteed provisioned GPUs.

SLA linkage
- Provisioned burst reservation guarantees best-effort capacity for the hosted fleet with a 95th percentile latency SLA for up to the reservation threshold. If capacity shortfall occurs (Redwood not able to honor reserved burst draw due to regional outage), credits are issued equal to the unused reservation fee for the impacted hours and an additional service credit up to 20% of the reservation for sustained failures. See attached provisioned-burst-sla.docx.
